topics.headline: Who actually holds the gavel on life
topics.blurb: House Judiciary writes the statutes. Energy & Commerce and Senate HELP oversee HHS and FDA. Appropriations LHHS and Senate Finance decide whether Medicaid and Title X dollars follow the policy.

committees.why: Abortion statutes, born-alive bills, and FACE Act enforcement.
HHS, FDA, and Medicaid abortion policy — Health subcommittee does the markups.
Labor-HHS appropriations: the rider fight over Hyde, Title X, and HHS grants.
Senate path for the same statutes and judicial nominees who will read them.
HELP oversees CDC, FDA, and most HHS health programs.
Finance writes Medicaid and Medicare — where most federal abortion-funding fights land.
Senate LHHS appropriations: same rider battlefield as the House.

topics.headline: Border policy is Homeland, Judiciary, and the money bills
topics.blurb: Homeland Security holds DHS and CBP. Judiciary writes immigration statute. Appropriations decides whether the agencies are staffed and fenced.

committees.why: DHS, CBP, and Border Patrol — Border Security subcommittee is the hearing room.
Immigration statute, interior enforcement, and asylum law.
Homeland Security appropriations: walls, agents, detention beds.
Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs — DHS oversight and border management.
Senate immigration statute and the Border Security subcommittee.
Senate DHS appropriations.

topics.headline: Guns move through Judiciary — and the ATF's budget
topics.blurb: House and Senate Judiciary write firearms law. Commerce-Justice-Science appropriations is where ATF and DOJ get fenced or funded.

committees.why: Firearms statutes, national reciprocity, and ATF oversight.
Senate path for the same bills and judicial nominees on Second Amendment cases.
CJS appropriations: ATF, FBI, and DOJ grant conditions.
Senate CJS appropriations — the other ATF lever.

topics.headline: Statute, tax code, and religious-liberty oversight
topics.blurb: Judiciary owns the civil-rights and religious-liberty statutes. Ways and Means and Finance own the tax treatment of marriage. Education committees hear the school and college fights.

committees.why: Religious Freedom Restoration Act, civil-rights statutes, and the Constitution subcommittee.
Senate Judiciary — same statutes and the nominees who will apply them.
Tax treatment of marriage and family in the code.
Senate Finance — joint filers, child tax credit, and family policy.
Campus and K-12 religious-liberty and curriculum fights.

topics.headline: Title IX, HHS rules, and the courts
topics.blurb: Education and Workforce is the Title IX committee. Energy & Commerce and HELP own the HHS/FDA medical rules. Judiciary is where definition-of-sex statutes and sports bills are marked up.

committees.why: Title IX, school sports, and campus rules.
HELP: HHS, pediatric gender medicine, and education statutes.
FDA and public-health rules; Health subcommittee holds the medical hearings.
Sex-definition statutes, Women's Bill of Rights, and prison/sports bills.
Senate path for the same bills.

topics.headline: Aid, diplomacy, and the intel product
topics.blurb: Foreign Affairs and Foreign Relations write the policy. State-Foreign Operations appropriations writes the check. Intelligence committees see the threat picture.

committees.why: Israel aid, sanctions, and the Abraham Accords oversight.
Senate Foreign Relations — treaties, nominations, and the same aid bills.
State and Foreign Operations appropriations: FMF and missile-defense dollars.
Senate SFOPS appropriations.
House Intelligence — Iran, Hamas, and Hezbollah reporting.
Senate Intelligence — the other half of that product.

topics.headline: Armed Services, Intelligence, and the China select
topics.blurb: HASC/SASC write the NDAA. Intelligence oversees the IC. Homeland covers the domestic edge. The China select is the 119th's dedicated CCP panel.

committees.why: NDAA, force design, and defense policy.
Senate Armed Services — the other NDAA chamber.
House Intelligence (HPSCI).
Senate Intelligence (SSCI).
Domestic terrorism, borders, and critical infrastructure.
Alliances, AUKUS, and China policy on the diplomatic side.
Select Committee on the CCP — the dedicated China panel.

topics.headline: Energy policy is E&C, ENR, and the spending bills
topics.blurb: House Energy & Commerce and Senate Energy write the statutes. EPW and Natural Resources own EPA and public lands. Energy and Water appropriations is the purse.

committees.why: Energy statute, EPA rules, and the Environment subcommittee.
Senate Energy and Natural Resources — federal lands and energy markets.
EPW: EPA, infrastructure, and climate bills.
Natural Resources — leasing, NEPA, and western lands.
Energy and Water appropriations: DOE and the labs.
Science Committee — climate research budgets and NOAA/NSF oversight.

topics.headline: Budget, tax, and the administrative state
topics.blurb: Budget sets the cap. Ways and Means and Finance write the code. Oversight and Judiciary's administrative-state subcommittee are where the agencies get cross-examined.

committees.why: House Budget Resolution — the spending ceiling.
Senate Budget.
Tax-writing committee. Article I, Section 7 starts here.
Senate Finance — the other tax-writing committee.
Oversight and Government Reform — agency waste and rulemaking.
Administrative State, Regulatory Reform, and Antitrust subcommittee.
House Appropriations — twelve bills that actually spend the money.

topics.headline: Curriculum is Education; civil-rights law is Judiciary
topics.blurb: Education and Workforce and Senate HELP own K-12 and college policy. Judiciary owns Title VI and the civil-rights statutes activists try to rewrite.

committees.why: K-12 curriculum, college accreditation, and Department of Education rules.
HELP — the Senate education committee, including the Education and the American Family subcommittee.
Title VI, disparate-impact doctrine, and civil-rights statutes.
Federal-agency DEI programs and contracting preferences.

topics.headline: Judiciary writes the code; CJS funds the cops
topics.blurb: House and Senate Judiciary own criminal law, sentencing, and DOJ oversight. Commerce-Justice-Science appropriations funds FBI, USMS, and Byrne JAG.

committees.why: Criminal code, sentencing, and the Crime subcommittee.
Senate Judiciary — Crime and Counterterrorism subcommittee.
CJS appropriations: FBI, COPS, and Byrne grants.
Senate CJS appropriations.

topics.headline: NDAA, defense appropriations, and veterans
topics.blurb: Armed Services writes the NDAA. Defense appropriations writes the check. Veterans' Affairs is the after-service committee. MILCON-VA is the facilities bill.

committees.why: House Armed Services — NDAA and force policy.
Senate Armed Services.
Defense appropriations — the largest discretionary bill.
Senate Defense appropriations.
House Veterans' Affairs.
Senate Veterans' Affairs.
Military Construction and VA appropriations.

topics.headline: Health markup is E&C, Ways and Means, HELP, and Finance
topics.blurb: House Energy & Commerce and Ways and Means split HHS and the tax side of health. Senate HELP and Finance are the matching pair. LHHS appropriations funds the agencies.

committees.why: Public health, FDA, Medicaid operations — Health subcommittee.
Medicare, tax exclusion for employer coverage, and health tax credits.
HELP — HHS agencies and private-insurance market rules.
Senate Finance — Medicare, Medicaid, and CHIP.
LHHS appropriations: NIH, CDC, and HHS grant accounts.
Senate LHHS appropriations.

topics.headline: AI is split across Judiciary, Science, Commerce, and Intel
topics.blurb: House Judiciary's AI subcommittee and Senate Privacy/Technology are the statute rooms. Science and Commerce own research and industry. Intelligence owns the national-security stack.

committees.why: Courts, IP, Artificial Intelligence, and the Internet subcommittee.
Privacy, Technology, and the Law — plus IP.
Science, Space, and Technology — federal AI research and NIST.
Senate Commerce — industry, NTIA, and Section 230-adjacent fights.
Communications and Technology subcommittee — the House telecom/AI overlap.
NSA and Cyber subcommittee — the classified AI stack.
